{"search_note":"I did not find direct 2024 evidence that Xi personally:
- overrode an ally/proxy/client to stop proliferation,
- punished a domestic faction specifically for pushing proliferation,
- or publicly took a hard line against a proliferation channel when it was politically convenient.

So the evidence is mostly policy-level and indirect, not a clean personal intervention record.","evidence":[{"title":"China's Non-Proliferation Policy and Measures","publisher":"PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs","date":"2024-06-06","url":"https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/wjb/zzjg_663340/jks_665232/kjlc_665236/fkswt_665240/202406/t20240606_11405135.html","summary":"China said it opposes WMD proliferation, has a legal and export-control system covering nuclear and missile-related items, and promotes peaceful resolution of the Korean Peninsula and Iran nuclear issues. This is the clearest broad nonproliferation-policy support.","question_ids":["1B.6","1B.4","1B.1"]},{"title":"Statement by H.E. Ambassador Cheng Jingye ... General Debate of the 61st Session of UNGA First Committee","publisher":"PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs","date":"2024-06-06","url":"https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/wjb/zzjg_663340/jks_665232/kjfywj_665252/202406/t20240606_11405245.html","summary":"China backed denuclearization of the Korean Peninsula and said it was opposed to proliferation of nuclear weapons on the Iranian file, while stressing diplomacy and arms-control mechanisms. This supports resistance to proliferation in official policy terms.","question_ids":["1B.6","1B.4"]},{"title":"Position Paper of the People's Republic of China For the 77th Session of the United Nations General Assembly","publisher":"PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs","date":"2024-05-31","url":"https://www.mfa.gov.cn/mfa_eng/zy/wjzc/202405/t20240531_11367524.html","summary":"China said it firmly opposes WMD proliferation and criticized AUKUS nuclear-submarine cooperation as undermining the NPT. That is direct nonproliferation signaling, though not a specific ally/proxy test.","question_ids":["1B.6","1B.4"]},{"title":"All Parties Reiterate to Fully and Effectively Implement the JCPOA on the Iranian Nuclear Issue","publisher":"PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs","date":"2024-06-06","url":"https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/wjb/zzjg_663340/xybfs_663590/xwlb_663592/202406/t20240606_11387067.html","summary":"China backed full JCPOA implementation and opposed dispute-escalation, which is consistent with resisting further Iranian nuclear advancement through diplomacy. The evidence is pro-restraint, not enforcement-heavy.","question_ids":["1B.6","1B.4"]},{"title":"Treasury Targets PRC-based Procurement Network Supporting DPRK Ballistic Missile and Space Programs","publisher":"U.S. Department of the Treasury","date":"2024-07-24","url":"https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/jy2482","summary":"Treasury sanctioned a PRC-based network for procuring items that supported DPRK ballistic missile and space programs. This is strong evidence that Chinese-based actors still enabled proliferation despite official policy.","question_ids":["1B.6","1B.1"]},{"title":"Chinese envoy: Pressure and power politics are not diplomacy, confrontation will not solve the Iran nuclear issue","publisher":"PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs","date":"2024-11-22","url":"https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/xw/zwbd/202412/t20241205_11538812.html","summary":"China voted against an IAEA resolution that would have increased pressure on Iran, arguing for diplomacy instead. That can be read as reluctance to confront a proliferating partner, even if framed as anti-escalatory.","question_ids":["1B.6","1B.4"]}]}
